title: Traction control light on
h1: Why is my traction control light on?
metaDesc: Traction or stability control light on or flashing? Find out in a few questions if it's normal, switched off, or a sensor fault, how urgent it is, and what to do next.
synonyms: traction control and abs light on
traction control and check engine light on
intro: The traction or stability control light (usually a car with wavy skid marks behind it) does two different jobs. A quick flash while driving on a slippery road usually means the system is working. A light that stays on usually means it's been switched off or has found a fault, and the other lights on the dash often help show why.
safety: If the red BRAKE light is on too, or the brake pedal feels soft, don't drive it until the brakes are checked.
If the check engine light is flashing and the engine shakes or runs rough, pull over safely and turn the engine off.
With traction or stability control off, slow down and leave extra room on wet, snowy or icy roads.

q_pattern.help: Depending on the car, it may be called TCS, ESC, ESP, VSC, VSA, DSC or StabiliTrak. They all control wheel spin and skids.

opts.a: It flickers briefly when I accelerate or turn on a wet, icy, snowy or gravel road, then goes out
It includes the word OFF, or it came on after a button was pressed
It flashes on dry roads, or the car cuts power or brakes a wheel for no reason

q_other_lights.q: Are any other warning lights on with it?

opts.a: The ABS light and the red BRAKE light
The check engine light is flashing, or the engine runs rough
The check engine light is on steadily

q_recent.q: Has any of this happened recently?

opts.a: New tires on only some wheels, a spare tire in use, or a tire that looks low
The battery was disconnected, replaced or jumped, or there was an alignment or steering work
Brake or wheel work, or a hard hit on a pothole or curb
None of these, or I'm not sure

result.title: The system is likely doing its job on a slippery road
result.now: Ease off the gas, steer smoothly, and slow down for the conditions. The light usually goes out once the tires have grip again.
if: If it flickers often on dry roads too, the tires may be worn or a sensor may be reading wrong. Get it checked.
If you're stuck in snow or mud, briefly turning traction control off can help you rock free. Turn it back on once you're moving.

If the light stays on steadily, or the ABS or check engine light comes on with it, the system may have a fault. Get it checked within a few days. If the red BRAKE light comes on, don't drive until the brakes are checked.
result.why: When a wheel starts to spin or the car starts to slide, the system brakes that wheel or cuts engine power for a moment. The light flickers to tell you it's stepping in, which means the road is slippery.

causes.name: Wheel spin on a slippery surface
causes.clues: It happens when pulling away or accelerating on wet, icy or loose roads.

causes.name: Worn tires
causes.clues: It happens often, even in light rain.

you: Check tread depth and tire pressures.

result.title: Traction or stability control has been switched off
result.now: Press the traction control button (often a car with skid marks and the word OFF) once, or turn the car off and restart it. Most systems turn back on at startup.
if: If the OFF light won't go out after a restart, the system may have a fault. Get it checked within a few days.
If the button is stuck or was pressed by something in the console, free it and try again.
If the ABS or red BRAKE light is also on, or the brake pedal feels different, don't drive until the brakes are checked.
result.why: Most cars let you switch traction control off, which is useful when stuck in snow or mud. The OFF light usually just shows it's switched off. It's easy to press the button by accident.

causes.name: Button pressed by accident
causes.clues: The light came on right after something touched the console or dash.

causes.name: Stuck button
causes.clues: The button feels sticky or doesn't spring back.

causes.name: System fault shown as OFF
causes.clues: The light stays on after a restart and the button doesn't change it.

you: Press the button and watch the light.

result.title: The system may be stepping in when it shouldn't, often from a bad sensor reading
result.now: Get the stability control system scanned within a few days. Until then, allow extra time when pulling into traffic, because the car may cut power without warning.
if: If the car cuts power or brakes hard on its own in traffic, stop driving it and have it towed.
If one tire is lower or a different size than the others, fix that first. It can confuse the system.
If the ABS or red BRAKE light comes on, or the brake pedal feels soft or different, don't drive it until the brakes are checked.
result.why: The system compares wheel speeds and steering angle to detect skids. If a sensor sends a wrong reading, or one tire spins at a different speed, the system can think the car is sliding and brake a wheel or cut power on a dry road. A shop will usually watch live sensor data on a test drive before replacing a sensor.

causes.name: Faulty wheel speed sensor
causes.clues: The ABS light comes on at times too.

causes.name: Mismatched or underinflated tire
causes.clues: One new tire, a spare in use, or the tire pressure light is on.

causes.name: Steering angle or yaw sensor reading wrong
causes.clues: It happens mostly in turns, or started after an alignment or battery work.

you: Check all four tire pressures and look for a mismatched tire.

result.title: Traction, ABS and red brake lights together can point to a brake system problem
result.now: Don't drive it. Check that the parking brake is fully released and look at the brake fluid level, then have it towed or call a mobile mechanic.
if: If the red BRAKE light goes out once the parking brake is fully released and the pedal feels normal, the ABS and traction lights still need checking within a day or two. If the red light stays on, keep the car parked.
If the brake fluid is low, topping it up doesn't make the car safe to drive, even if you can't see a leak. Have the brakes inspected before driving.
If the brake pedal feels soft, sinks toward the floor, or needs much more force, don't drive the car.
result.why: Traction and stability control rely on the ABS system. When the red brake light joins them, fluid may be low or the system that balances front and rear braking may not be working. The car can skid or spin in a hard stop, and low fluid can also mean a leak or very worn brakes.

causes.name: Low brake fluid
causes.clues: Fluid at or below the MIN mark, or wet spots near a wheel.

causes.name: ABS module or wheel speed sensor fault
causes.clues: Fluid level is normal and the pedal feels normal.

causes.name: Parking brake not fully released
causes.clues: The red light goes out when you release it fully.

you: Make sure the parking brake is fully released.
Check the brake fluid level with the engine off.
shop: ABS and brake system code scan

result.title: A wheel speed sensor fault may have switched off ABS and traction control
result.now: Get the ABS codes read within the next few days. Until then, brake earlier and leave extra room, especially in rain or snow, and pay attention to how the brakes feel.
if: If the red BRAKE light comes on, or the pedal feels soft, sinks or needs more force, stop driving it.
If you hear grinding, smell burning from a wheel, or the car pulls when braking, have it checked before driving further.
If the lights came on right after brake or wheel work, contact the shop that did it. A sensor or connector may have been disturbed, and they can check it.
result.why: Traction control, stability control and ABS all use the same wheel speed sensors. When one stops sending a signal, the car switches these systems off and lights the warnings. Regular braking is designed to keep working without ABS, but the wheels can lock in a hard stop, so allow more distance. A shop will usually check live sensor data and the wiring before replacing a sensor.

causes.name: Failed wheel speed sensor
causes.clues: A common cause, especially on older cars in salty areas.

causes.name: Damaged sensor wiring
causes.clues: Recent brake or suspension work, or a pothole hit.

causes.name: ABS module fault
causes.clues: All sensors test fine.

you: Look behind each wheel for a loose connector or dangling wire.

result.title: The engine may be misfiring, and traction control has shut off as a result
result.now: Pull over safely and turn the engine off. Have the car towed or call a mobile mechanic.
if: If you smell fuel or see smoke, get everyone out and away from the car.
If the temperature gauge is high or the oil pressure light is on, don't restart the engine.
result.why: A flashing check engine light usually means a misfire bad enough to overheat and damage the catalytic converter. Many cars switch traction control off when the engine has a serious fault, because they can't control engine power reliably.

causes.name: Failed ignition coil or spark plug
causes.clues: Shaking at idle or when accelerating.

causes.name: Fuel injector problem
causes.clues: Rough running with a fuel smell.

causes.name: Serious engine mechanical problem
causes.clues: Knocking, or loss of coolant or oil.

result.title: An engine fault may have switched off traction control
result.now: Have the engine codes read within a few days. Many auto parts stores can read basic codes for you.
if: If the check engine light starts flashing or the engine runs rough, pull over and stop driving.
If the temperature gauge climbs toward the red or the oil pressure light comes on, pull over and turn the engine off.
If the car goes into a low-power mode, have it checked before relying on it. Low power can make merging and passing dangerous.
result.why: Traction control works partly by reducing engine power. When the engine computer finds a fault, many cars switch traction control off as a precaution. Fixing the engine fault often turns the traction light off too.

causes.name: Engine sensor or emissions fault
causes.clues: The engine runs normally, and the check engine light is steady.

causes.name: Throttle or accelerator pedal sensor fault
causes.clues: Hesitation, or a low-power mode.

causes.name: Shared wiring or voltage problem
causes.clues: Several other lights flicker, or the battery is weak.

you: Get the engine codes read with a code reader.
shop: Engine and stability control code scan

result.title: The steering angle sensor may need to be reset or calibrated
result.now: Check your owner's manual for a reset step, such as turning the wheel fully left and right with the engine running. If that doesn't work, book a calibration.
if: If the light came on after an alignment, ask the alignment shop to calibrate the sensor. It's a normal part of the job on many cars.
If the car brakes a wheel or cuts power on its own, especially in turns, stop driving it and have it checked.
If the ABS or red BRAKE light comes on, or the steering feels different, have it checked before driving further.
result.why: Stability control needs to know where the steering wheel is pointed. After the battery is disconnected or the wheels are aligned, some cars lose that setting and turn the light on until the sensor is reset.

causes.name: Steering angle sensor lost calibration
causes.clues: The light came on right after battery or alignment work.

causes.name: Steering wheel off-center after an alignment
causes.clues: The wheel isn't straight when you drive straight.

causes.name: Faulty steering angle sensor
causes.clues: Calibration doesn't fix it.

you: Try the reset steps in the owner's manual.
Notice whether the steering wheel is straight when driving straight.

result.title: Mismatched or low tires can confuse the system
result.now: Check all four tire pressures and set them to the door-sticker values. If a compact spare is on, get the regular tire back on soon.
if: If the light stays on after the tires are matched and inflated, get a stability control scan.
If only two tires were replaced, ask the tire shop whether the tire sizes and wear levels are close enough for your car, especially if it's all-wheel drive.
If you see a bulge, cut or cords on a tire, or the ABS or red BRAKE light comes on, don't drive until it's checked.
result.why: The system compares how fast each wheel turns. A low tire, a smaller spare, or tires with very different wear spin at a different speed, which can look like wheel slip and turn the light on.

causes.name: Underinflated tire
causes.clues: The tire pressure light is on, or one tire looks low.

causes.name: Compact spare in use
causes.clues: A smaller temporary spare is on the car.

causes.name: Mismatched tire sizes or wear
causes.clues: Only some tires were replaced.

you: Compare the size printed on each tire's sidewall.
shop: Tire size and tread depth check

result.title: Traction and stability control may have switched off because of a fault
result.now: Get the stability control and ABS codes read within the next few days. Until then, drive more gently, leave extra room, especially on slippery roads, and pay attention to how the brakes feel.
if: If the ABS or red BRAKE light comes on, or the brakes feel different, stop driving it.
If the check engine light starts flashing or the engine runs rough, pull over and turn it off.
If the car brakes a wheel or cuts power on its own, stop driving it and have it checked.
If the check engine light comes on steadily too, mention it. Fixing the engine fault may clear the traction light.
result.why: A steady traction or stability light without the word OFF usually means the system found a fault and turned itself off. The car won't get the system's help if a wheel spins or the car starts to slide. A scan shows which sensor or circuit to test next.

causes.name: Wheel speed sensor fault
causes.clues: A common cause. The ABS light may come on too.

causes.name: Steering angle sensor fault or calibration
causes.clues: Recent battery, steering or alignment work.

causes.name: Engine or throttle fault
causes.clues: The check engine light is on, or the engine feels sluggish.

you: Note any other lights on the dash.
